service.description: Starts the task number sequence of a project (Project_KEY, which TaskServices.create#Task numbers its tasks KEY-n from, a bank of 1 so there are no gaps) after lastTaskNum, so the first new task is lastTaskNum + 1. A project whose sequence is already started (an existing project, or a key used before) keeps it. In its own transaction: a sequence refill reads the row on another connection and would wait on an uncommitted insert.

What a client contact who signs in sees (design-projects.md §1.1; impl-projects.md P10), for userId (the current user when empty). isClient: the user holds the PROJECT_CLIENT permission (an app's client group grants it); every other output is empty when not. A client's projects are the projects (not templates) that allow client sign-in (their WorkEffortSetting WstClientSignIn Y; there is no organization default) on which the user's party, or an organization the person is a current contact, employee or representative of (PartyRelationship PrtContact, PrtEmployee or PrtRepresentative from the person), holds a current client role (Customer, CustomerBillTo, ClientManager, ClientBilling): - clientProjectIds: those projects; clientOrgIds: those of the organizations that are a client of one of them; clientPartyIds: the user's party and clientOrgIds; clientContactPartyIds: the user's party and the current contacts, employees and representatives of clientOrgIds (whose requests are their organization's); - shareHoursProjectIds and shareRepositoryProjectIds: those that share their hours (WstShareHours, the project's or its organization's billing default) or their repositories (WstShareRepositories) with the client; - statusUpdateIds: the communication events of the status updates posted for the client on them (WorkEffortUpdate clientVisible Y); - scopePartyIds: the parties a client may know of: clientContactPartyIds, clientOrgIds, the owners of its projects and the current parties of them and of their items shared with the client, and the parties of their requests. Strict: anything that fails is an error, so a caller deciding access refuses.

Puts what a client contact sees (get#ClientProjectInfo) in the user context for the entity filters of an app's client group (IronStone's BOSS_PROJECT_CLIENT filter set; impl-projects.md F2), as setup#UserOrganizationInfo does for the organization filters; called per render from an app root's always-actions. clientUser is true for a client; each list holds _NA_ when empty, so a filter on it matches nothing. A failure leaves the user a client with empty lists.

The projects the current user may see, as what a find of projects, tasks, requests or time applies as a condition (no entity filter covers WorkEffort, Request or TimeEntry): - allProjects: true for the ADMIN group, which sees every project; the lists below then do not limit a find. - visibleProjectIds: the projects the user holds a current WorkEffortParty role on (memberProjectIds), and the projects with visibility All users or General (WevAllUsers, WevGeneral) of the user's organizations (orgIds: the filterOrgIds of PartyServices.get#PartyOrganizationInfo, the active organization when one is set): owned by one (ownerPartyId) or with one in a current role (as the Vendor). A project in Work group, Restricted or Confidential, or with no visibility, is seen only by its parties. - managedProjectIds: those the user is ProjectManager or Manager of, and restrictedItemIds: the Restricted and Confidential tasks the user holds a current role on. A Restricted or Confidential task is seen only by its own parties and the managers of its project. So a find of projects applies workEffortId in visibleProjectIds; a find of tasks applies rootWorkEffortId in visibleProjectIds and (visibilityEnumId not in WevRestricted, WevConfidential, or rootWorkEffortId in managedProjectIds, or workEffortId in restrictedItemIds); each unless allProjects. Four small finds, so a screen may call it on each render. - A client contact who signs in (the PROJECT_CLIENT permission, get#ClientProjectInfo; impl-projects.md P10) sees only its client projects (visibleProjectIds), is a member or manager of none and sees no Restricted item, whatever its groups (ADMIN too): isClient is true and itemVisibilityIds holds the visibilities of the items it sees (WevAllUsers, WevGeneral: shared with the client), which a find of tasks applies as well (visibilityEnumId in itemVisibilityIds). itemVisibilityIds is null for everyone else.
Sets a project's own value of a setting (a WorkEffortSettingType); an empty value removes the project's row, so the organization's applies again (get#ProjectSettings).

A project's settings by WorkEffortSettingType: its own WorkEffortSetting rows, else the organization's. The organization is organizationPartyId, else the project's owner when an organization, else its current Vendor. Its setting is the PartySetting the type's optionValue names (a Projects app setting, ProjBillingDefaults and the like), a JSON object whose enumCode key holds the value (a boolean as Y or N); a type without an optionValue has no organization default. An app setting that is not a JSON object is logged and skipped. settingSources tells for each value where it came from: project or organization.

A project's numbers against its caps. projectDanger: the actual client cost past the client budget, or the actual and remaining hours past the estimate (only when the project has an estimate: a project with time and no estimate is not in danger, impl-projects.md F70); projectWarning: less of the estimate done than of the client budget used.
Gets statistics for project milestones

actions.script: for (const statsField of statsFields) milestoneStatsTotals[statsField] = toDecimal(0)

service.description: Work items (WetTask) as the work item tree shows them (design-projects.md §5 "The work item tree", style-guide §3.15), one level per call (impl-projects.md F13), each row with its subtree's roll-up: - parentWorkEffortId: its children; topLevel with rootWorkEffortId: the project's items with no parent; or workEffortIds (a list or comma text): those items, and with withAncestors each one's ancestors up to the top (first, from the top down), so the matches of a find sit in their place. - A level is in rank order (sequenceNum, then the number of the key); statusId (comma list) narrows it. - Each row has the work effort's fields, childCount (its children the user sees), depth (0 at the top) and the roll-up of itself and its descendants, cancelled items and their subtrees left out (as get#WorkEffortChildStats sums them): totalEstimatedWorkTime, totalRemainingWorkTime, totalActualWorkTime, totalBudget (the totalTimeAllowed of the subtree), totalEstimatedPoints, itemCount and doneCount (descendants, and those Complete or Closed), percentDone (estimate less remaining over estimate, 0 to 100, null with no estimate). - totals: the same sums over the rows returned that are not an ancestor added for them. Only items the user may see (get#VisibleProjectInfo, impl-projects.md F1): of a project the user sees, a Restricted or Confidential one only for its parties and the project's managers; an item of no project for its owner and parties. Items of a project are read once per project, so the roll-ups of a level cost one find of the project.

What the Timeline draws (design-projects.md §5 Timeline, §15 Timeline data; impl-projects.md P4c): - itemList: the work items of workEffortIds (a find's items, a list or comma text) with, by withAncestors, their ancestors up to the top so the tree holds them (ancestor true), each as get#WorkItemTree gives it (only items the user may see, depth, childCount, the roll-up) plus startDay and dueDay (its own estimated start and due, days yyyy-MM-dd in the user's time zone), spanStartDay and spanDueDay (the earliest start and latest due of it and its sub-items at every depth, cancelled ones aside: a parent's summary bar), progress (0 to 100: 100 when done, else the roll-up's estimate less remaining over estimate, else the done of its sub-items), isDone, and its plan items (milestoneId, releaseId, sprintId, componentId). - dependencyList: the current WeatDependsOn between the items, {workEffortId (the dependent), toWorkEffortId (what it waits for), lagDays, violated: it starts (or is due) before the next weekday after the other's due plus the lag}. - planItemList: the milestones, releases and sprints of the items' projects (and of rootWorkEffortId), not cancelled, {workEffortId, kind (milestone, release, sprint), workEffortName, rootWorkEffortId, statusId, startDay, dueDay, actualCompletionDay, percentDone (get#PlanItemSummary), itemCount, doneCount}.
Gets statistics for direct children WorkEfforts plus their descendants

service.description: The id of a new plan item of a project: KEY-MS-n for a milestone, KEY-REL-n for a release, KEY-CMP-n for a component, n one past the highest of the kind and free of other records.

A milestone, release or component of a project (create#Milestone, create#Release, create#Component): the id given (refused when taken) or the next of get#PlanItemDefaults; a name (a release's version, which no other release of the project has); dates (the due date not before the start).
A milestone of a project (WetMilestone, In Planning unless statusId says otherwise), id KEY-MS-n unless given; with a start date it marks a phase (create#PlanItem).

service-call.name: mantle.work.ProjectServices.create#PlanItem

service.description: A release of a project (WetRelease, In Planning), id KEY-REL-n unless given: its name is the version (as 1.4.0), which no other release of the project has; its due date is the planned release date (create#PlanItem). A tag named as the version, or v and the version, links to it (GitServices.link#RefByName).

service-call.name: mantle.work.ProjectServices.create#PlanItem

service.description: A component of a project (WetComponent), id KEY-CMP-n unless given (create#PlanItem).

A plan item's (a milestone, release or component) name, description, dates and status; a parameter not given is left as it is, and clearFields (a list or comma text of description, estimatedStartDate, estimatedCompletionDate) empties those. A release keeps a version no other release of its project has; the due date is not before the start. A status moves by the Default flow. A milestone whose gate requires approval (WstApprovalRequired Y) is not reached (Complete or Closed) until its latest request is approved (approve#MilestoneApproval reaches it).

The progress of plan items (milestones, releases, sprints, components) from their current work items: by plan item id, itemCount (not counting cancelled ones), doneCount (Complete or Closed), inProgressCount, notStartedCount (In Planning or Approved), cancelledCount, percentDone (done of the counted, whole percent), the hours (estimated, remaining and actual: estimatedWorkTime, remainingWorkTime, actualWorkTime), hoursPercent ((estimated − remaining) of estimated), and the points (estimatedPoints, donePoints). An item in the plan item and also its sub-items counts each of them.

A draft of a release's notes, markdown (design-projects.md §15 Release notes): the release's description, then its done items (Complete or Closed) by type, Features (new features and enhancements), Fixes and Other, each with its key and title in key order (openCount: how many are not done yet, which the notes leave out); then its merged merge requests (those linked to its items, WorkEffortGitMergeRequest), of the repositories the user may view. The notes have no title of their own: title is the version and the date (released, else planned).

A release's notes as kept (its WorkEffortContent of type WectReleaseNotes; empty when none yet), when they changed, and the page they are published as (WikiPageWorkEffort of the release: wikiPageId, wikiSpaceId, pagePath).
Keeps a release's notes (markdown) as its WorkEffortContent of type WectReleaseNotes, a file under the content root (mantle.content.root) at work/releaseId/release-notes.md.

Publishes a release's notes (notesText, which is kept first; else those kept; else a generated draft), each way on its own (one that fails is a warning naming it, and the others still go): toDocs, a page named as the version under the page Releases of the project's documentation space (WstDocsWikiSpace; Releases is made when missing), its title the project and version and the date, a new version of it when it is there already, linked to the release by WikiPageWorkEffort; toChangelog, the section of the version at the top of CHANGELOG.md (made when missing; a section of the version already there is replaced) in repositoryId, a repository of the project (by default the first the user may update), committed by the user (org.moqui.impl.GitServices.commit#GitFiles, which checks the right to update); notify, the topic ReleasePublished to the followers of the release and of the project (but the user).

Releases a release that is not complete (design-projects.md §4 ReleaseDetail, Release): its items not done (not Complete, Closed or Cancelled) move to moveUnfinishedTo, next (the default: the next open release of the project by its planned date; none when there is none), none (out of any release) or a release id of the project that is open; then it is Complete with today as its date. Then, each on its own (one that fails is a warning, and the release stands): with createTag, a tag (tagName, by default v and the version when the version starts with a digit, else the version) at revision (the default branch's head when empty) in repositoryId, a repository of the project, linked to the release; with publish (the default), the notes (notesText, else kept, else a draft) to the documentation space when the project has one, CHANGELOG.md with toChangelog, and the followers with notify.

A project's documentation space, named in its setting WstDocsWikiSpace: storage repository, rooted at git://repositoryId/docs in a repository of the project the user may update (pages are markdown files under docs/ beside the code, each save a commit on the default branch; impl-projects.md F7), or db (database files). Its id is wikiSpaceId, else the project's key (P and the key when it starts with a digit), else the key with DOCS, DOC or WIKI, the first that is free (3 to 8 letters, digits or _). Members only (restrictView) unless the project is seen by all users or is General; only members change it (restrictUpdate); its users follow the project's internal members (sync#ProjectDocsSpaceUsers), the user who makes it administers it. A project with a space keeps it.

The users of a project's documentation space (WstDocsWikiSpace, the project's own setting) follow its internal members (WorkEffortParty now, not the client roles; client access is impl-projects.md P10): each member's user views and edits it, and administers it when a ProjectManager or Manager; a user no longer a member loses a row that does not administer the space. Run by the rule on WorkEffortParty (Work.eecas.xml) and when the space is made; nothing for a work effort with no space. One user that fails is logged and the others go on.

What a new sprint of a project starts with (SprintForm): its number (n of the id KEY-SP-n, one past the highest), the name Sprint n, the start the next weekday after the latest sprint ends (else today), the end two weeks after the latest sprint's end (else 13 days after the start), the last end moved back to a Friday when it falls on a weekend, as yyyy-MM-dd; the project's estimate unit (hours or points) and its sprints' latest capacity.

A sprint of a project (WetSprint, In Planning), id KEY-SP-n; the name, dates and capacity default as get#SprintDefaults gives them. The goal is the description; the capacity is in the project's estimate unit.
A sprint's name, goal (description), dates and capacity (in the project's estimate unit); an empty capacity clears it. A parameter not given is left as it is.

Begins a planned sprint (In Planning, or Approved): In Progress from now (actualStartDate), with new dates or goal when given. Refused while another sprint of the project is in progress, naming it, unless the project allows several (WstSeveralSprints Y, for teams sharing a project). The items in the sprint now are its commitment.

Ends a sprint in progress: Complete from now (actualCompletionDate). Its items that are done (Complete or Closed) and cancelled stay in it; the rest are carried over, their membership ending at the completion: to carryToSprintId (a planned or active sprint of the project), else by carryTo: next (the default: the next planned sprint by its start, a new one when there is none), new (a new sprint, newSprintName or the default name) or backlog (no sprint).

A status update of a project (design-projects.md §4 ProjectOverview PostUpdate, §15 Project health): the message, a CommunicationEvent of type StatusUpdate from the user on the project's Chatter (WorkEffortCommEvent); the WorkEffortUpdate row with the health, the percent complete and whether it is posted for the client; and the project's healthEnumId, which follows the latest update. The project's internal members with a user, not the one posting, are told on the topic ProjectStatusUpdate; an update posted for the client (clientVisible Y) is also emailed to the project's client contacts (send#ProjectUpdateEmail: on a project with client sign-in only); a notification or an email that fails is logged, not the update's.

Whom a project's client is told by email (impl-projects.md P10b, F101): the people (PtyPerson) holding a current client role on the project (Customer, CustomerBillTo, ClientManager, ClientBilling), each with its primary email address (get#PrimaryEmailAddress), and not one whose user accounts are all disabled; partyIds narrows to those. A person without an address is in skippedList. clientSignIn: the project lets its client sign in (WstClientSignIn Y). fromAddress and fromName: the project's organization (its owner, else its Vendor) and its primary email address, else senderPartyId's address under that name. Reads with authorization off; the callers decide what is sent.

Emails a status update posted for the client (its WorkEffortUpdate clientVisible Y) to the project's client contacts (get#ProjectClientContacts), each its own message by template MANTLE_PROJECT_UPDATE: the project, the health, the percent complete, the update's subject and text, nothing else (no internal note, member, money or link to an internal screen). Only on a project that lets its client sign in (WstClientSignIn Y), so the email tells the client no more than it reads signed in. Each email on its own (failure tolerance): one that fails is logged and in skippedList. Called by post#ProjectUpdate.

What moved in a project (design-projects.md §15 Project activity), newest first and paged: the status changes of the project and its work items from the entity audit log, the comments, messages and status updates on them (WorkEffortCommEvent), and the commits linked to its items (WorkEffortGitCommit). A Restricted or Confidential item is left out unless the user is one of its parties or manages the project (get#VisibleProjectInfo). Each source stands alone: one that fails is logged, named in failedSources and left out. The caller checks that the user may see the project. An entry is {kind (status, comment, update or commit), date, workEffortId and workEffortName (the item, or the project), title (what changed, in words), text (a comment's start, a commit's summary), authorName, userId, communicationEventId or commitId}.

parameter.name: kinds
parameter.description: A comma list of status, comment, update, commit; empty is all

service.description: The counters of Projects Home for the current user (design-projects.md §3 Home Counters, §15 Project home and Today services), over the projects the user sees (get#VisibleProjectInfo; template projects left out): - myOpen: the open work items the user is an Assignee of; dueWeek: those due from today through seven days; overdue: those due before today (as WorkItems' smart lists mine, week and overdue); - reviewsWaiting: the open merge requests of the repositories the user may view where the user is a requested reviewer who has not reviewed yet (org.moqui.impl.GitReviewServices.find#MergeRequests waitingForUserId); null when the build has no git hosting; - hoursWeek: the hours of the user's time entries this week (the week of the user's timesheet policy, TimesheetServices.get#WeekRange), with expectedWeek (the week's working hours) and timesheetStatusId (TmshInProcess when the week has no timesheet yet) beside the counts; - with managers: projectsAtRisk, the open projects the user manages (ADMIN: all) whose health is At risk or Off track or whose numbers warn (get#ProjectStats projectWarning or projectDanger), and milestonesSoon, their open milestones due in fourteen days. - with managers, timesheetsToApprove: the submitted timesheets the user approves (TimesheetServices.find#Timesheets list toApprove). - with managers, allocationRequests: the requested allocations of the projects the user sees, for one who approves allocations (ADMIN or ALLOCATION_APPROVE; ResourceServices.find#Allocations list requested), else null. - with managers, unbilledAmount: the amount of the billable time not invoiced in the projects the user sees (get#UnbilledSummary totals amount, a BigDecimal, with unbilledCurrencyUomId; null in more than one currency), for one who manages money (ADMIN or TIME_ENTRY_RATE), else null. Each counter is computed on its own: one that fails is logged, named in failedParts and left null.

What waits to be billed to clients (design-projects.md §10 Unbilled, §4 ProjectMoney UnbilledBox, §3 Home's Unbilled; impl-projects.md P8a), for those who manage money (ADMIN and holders of TIME_ENTRY_RATE; anyone else gets an error), over the projects they see (get#VisibleProjectInfo; every project for ADMIN; templates left out), or one project (workEffortId) or one client's (clientPartyId).
Unbilled time is a billable entry (rate type not RatpNoCharge) with no client invoice (invoiceId) that has ended (thruDate) by thruDate (default now), on the project or one of its items. Its amount is hours times its client hour rate (clientHourRate, else the rate of its rateAmountId), rounded to the cent per entry as an invoice of an item per entry totals it; an entry with neither is counted in missingRateCount and has no amount (invoicing it fails until a rate is found). Ready time is on an approved timesheet (TmshApproved): what create#ProjectInvoiceItems with approvedOnly bills.
projectList, by client then project, each: workEffortId, workEffortName, clientPartyId and clientName (the current Customer or CustomerBillTo), vendorPartyId (Vendor or VendorBillFrom), currencyUomId (the entries' rates', else the organization's base, else USD), entryCount, hours, amount, readyCount, readyHours, readyAmount, waitingHours (on a submitted timesheet), openHours (on an open one), missingRateCount, readyMissingRateCount, firstDate and lastDate (millis of the entries' fromDate), expenseCount and expenseAmount (the project's expense invoices paid and not billed through, which a client invoice adds), lastInvoiceId and lastInvoiceDate (the project's latest client invoice not cancelled), draftInvoiceList (its In-Process invoices to the client: invoiceId, invoiceDate, invoiceTotal), and milestoneDueList (the milestone billing shares due: reached, approved when gated, not billed; get#MilestoneBilling: workEffortId, milestoneName, orderId, orderItemSeqId, itemDescription, percent, invoicePercent, amount, currencyUomId, reachedDate), milestoneDueCount and milestoneDueAmount (a project with only shares due is listed too), timeReady (approved time to invoice and each with a rate), and canInvoice with cannotReason (no client, no vendor, nothing ready: no approved time and no share due, a ready entry without a rate). With withEntries also entryList (each entry: timeEntryId, partyId, personName, workEffortId, workEffortName, fromDate, thruDate, hours, rate, amount, ready, sheetStatusId, comments, missingRate), for one project's invoice dialog.
totals: projectCount, entryCount, hours, amount, readyHours, readyAmount, missingRateCount, currencyUomId (null when the projects bill in more than one currency, mixedCurrency then true and amount and readyAmount null) and byClient (clientPartyId, clientName, hours, amount), largest first. Amounts are BigDecimal. Reads only: no rate is looked up or stored here.

The today-source of IronStone Projects (design-projects.md §1.4 and §15 Project home and Today services; Projects.xml shell-providers; mantle.work.WorkEffortServices.get#UserTodayItems calls it with userId, partyId, fromDate and thruDate), for the current user: the running timer (kind timer, its item as the record, startDate when it started, timeEntryId to stop it); merge requests waiting for the user's review (kind review, the merge request as the record; none without git hosting in the build); the user's timesheets to submit (kind timesheet, the timesheet as the record, weekStart and hours): this week's from the last working day of the week, and any older one of the last eight weeks still In-Process with time on it (overdue; a returned one says so); and the new requests in the projects the user triages (kind triage, requestId, the project as the record: Submitted with no assignee, where the user is the project's triage assignee, else one of its managers when it names none). Work items due reach Today already through WorkEffortParty. Each part stands alone: one that fails is logged and left out.

The project templates (design-projects.md §12 Templates, §15 Template flag: WorkEffort isTemplate Y) by name, each with its counts: work items, milestones, members (current WorkEffortParty rows) and the projects made from it (WorkEffortAssoc WeatBasedOn, which clone#Project writes). Those of organizationPartyId (its owner, or a current party of it) when given, and those with no owner.

A project template (design-projects.md §12 Templates NewTemplate, §4 ProjectSettings TemplateBox): a copy of baseWorkEffortId kept as a template (clone#Project with isTemplate Y: its tree, members, settings and files, the dates cleared and the items back in planning), or with no base a blank one (create#Project, isTemplate Y). The template has the base's owner, else ownerPartyId.

matches.message: Project ID must be only letters and digits and between 1 and 8 characters long

service.description: A milestone (WetMilestone) of a project the user sees, its gate and what the user may do: canView, canRequest (a current party of the project, one who manages it, a holder of MILESTONE_APPROVE, ADMIN), canDecide (the approver's own user; or, recording it for the approver, one who manages the project, a holder of MILESTONE_APPROVE, ADMIN), canSetGate (one who manages the project, MILESTONE_APPROVE, ADMIN), isApprover. gate: required, approverPartyId, approverName, the latest request (approval: its fields, with statusId) and approved (the latest request approved), awaiting (the latest requested). An error "not available" when the user does not see it, unless need is none.

A milestone's gate: whether reaching it needs approval (approvalRequired Y or N) and the approver, a party with a current role on the project (a manager or a client contact); by one who manages the project. A gate is not taken off while a request waits (cancel it first).

Asks the approver of a gated milestone to approve it (a WorkEffortApproval, Requested): by the project's team; the milestone open (not reached, closed or cancelled) and no request waiting. workEffortContentId: the file to approve (the estimate). The approver's users get MilestoneApproval in the tray (a client contact has none until impl-projects.md P10: the manager then records the decision).

The approver's approval of a milestone's waiting request (workEffortApprovalId, or the milestone's waiting one by workEffortId), by the approver's user or recorded for them (get#MilestoneApprovalAccess canDecide): the request Approved, then the milestone reached (Complete) when open. When it is the project's Estimate milestone, the project moves from In Planning to Approved and its open or proposed sales orders (OrderItemWorkEffort) to Approved. All in one transaction.
The approver's refusal of a milestone's waiting request, with the reason (required), by the approver's user or recorded for them; the milestone stays open and a new request may follow.
Withdraws a milestone's waiting request (as a new estimate replaces the one sent), by the project's team.

The notices of a milestone's approval (requested: MilestoneApproval to the approver's users; approved, refused and cancelled: MilestoneDecision to the one who asked, not the one deciding), with workEffortId, milestoneName, rootWorkEffortId, projectName, approverName, requesterName, actorName, decision and reasonSuffix; a decision marks the open approval notices of the request decided. A failure is logged and the change stays.

A project's estimate (design-projects.md §14 Project estimate): the work breakdown from the top-level items down to depth (1 to 4, default 2), each line with its roll-up estimate in hours (a leaf's estimatedWorkTime, a parent's the sum of its children's; cancelled items left out) and its amount at the project's client rate (mantle.work.TimeServices.find#RateAmount: the standard client rate of the project, for no one in particular); the milestones with their due dates; the project's order lines (OrderItemWorkEffort); the totals. estimateHtml: the printed estimate (escaped), which the Estimate milestone keeps as its file when sent for approval. For one who manages money (ADMIN, TIME_ENTRY_RATE) and sees the project.

Sends a project's estimate for approval (design-projects.md §4 ProjectMoney, §14): its printed estimate (get#ProjectEstimate at depth) saved as a file (WectEstimate, an html document under the content root at work/milestoneId/) of the project's Estimate milestone (its WstEstimateMilestone; made when missing, In Progress, with a gate whose approver is the project's ClientManager, else its Customer), any request waiting on it withdrawn, and its gate's approval requested with the file; the project's open sales orders become Proposed (a quote). By one who manages money and manages the project (get#MilestoneApprovalAccess canSetGate on the milestone). Refused when the project has no client. When the approver is a client contact (a person with a client role on the project, get#ProjectClientContacts) the estimate is also emailed to it (send#EstimateEmail); an email that fails is logged, and the estimate stays sent.

Emails a project's estimate sent for approval to its approver when the approver is a client contact (get#ProjectClientContacts: a person with a current client role on the project and an email address; an organization or an internal approver is not emailed, the gate's notice tells its users): template MANTLE_PROJECT_ESTIMATE, the sender's comments, the printed estimate (estimateHtml, as get#ProjectEstimate made it and the milestone's file keeps it) in the message and as an attached html file, and that it is approved through the milestone's gate. Nothing else: no internal note, member or money the estimate does not show. One that fails is logged and in skippedList (failure tolerance). Called by send#EstimateForApproval.

The billing shares of milestones (design-projects.md §4 MilestoneBilling, MilestoneBillingShare; §10 MilestonesDue): each OrderItemWorkEffort of a milestone (one milestone by workEffortId, a project's by rootWorkEffortId, an order's by orderId) with invoicePercent or invoiceAmount: the milestone (name, status, reached date, gate required and approved), the order line (orderId, orderItemSeqId, description, its total, currency, the order's status), the share (percent, amount: the fixed amount, else the percent of the line's total, rounded to the cent), billed (invoiceId, invoiceItemSeqId, invoice status: a WorkEffortBilling not cancelled with the line's OrderItemBilling) and due (reached, its gate approved when required, not billed). lineList: the order lines linked to the project or the milestones (orderId, orderItemSeqId, description, total, sharedPercent, sharedAmount, billedAmount). For those who manage money (ADMIN, TIME_ENTRY_RATE) and see the project; else an error.

A milestone's billing share of an order line (OrderItemWorkEffort invoicePercent or invoiceAmount), or with remove the share taken off. The line is the project's (linked to the project or one of its milestones, or a line of a sales order to the project's client); the shares of a line total at most the line's total; a percent is over 0 and at most 100, an amount over 0; a billed share is not changed. By one who manages money and manages the project.

The order line a project fulfils (design-projects.md §4 ProjectMoneyStep, Commercial; §10 OrderDetail): an OrderItemWorkEffort of the project and a line of a sales order to the project's client (OrderPart customerPartyId), not cancelled; with remove the link is taken off (refused while its milestones' shares on the line are billed: they are taken off with it otherwise). By one who manages money and manages the project.

A project's money (design-projects.md §4 ProjectMoney BudgetActuals, ProjectInvoices, ProjectExpenses, Commercial): the caps (hours budget totalTimeAllowed, client budget totalClientCostAllowed) against the actuals (estimated, actual and remaining hours from get#ProjectStats; the time's cost at the workers' rates actualCost and its value at the client rates actualClientCost, rolled up from the time; profit; budget used and remaining); what was billed (the project's client invoices not cancelled: invoiced, paid, open; a list of them), the expenses (expense invoices on the project: total, billed through), the unbilled time (get#UnbilledSummary), the order lines and the milestone shares (get#MilestoneBilling: contracted, shared, billed, due). BigDecimal amounts in currencyUomId. For those who manage money and see the project; else an error.
